characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Tauros relies on relentless physical charges, whipping itself into a frenzy with its three tails before barrelling headfirst into opponents. It fights with overwhelming momentum and blunt force.

mechanisms: Sturdy physique to absorb kinetic impacts
Intimidate ability to lower opponent's attack power

limitations: Becomes confused after using rampage moves like Thrash
Charges blindly, making it predictable and susceptible to evasion

sources.supports: Combat techniques, physical offense style, and weaknesses

feats.claim: Smashes through thick stone walls and trees during a blind charge.
feats.citation: Pokémon anime episode: 'Showdown at Dark City'

notableResults.note: Pikachu used agility and electric counterattacks.

unknowns: Exact top speed during a full-force charge across varying terrain.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Tentacool floats in aquatic environments or drifts along shores, using its poisonous tentacles to sting and weaken attackers from a distance. It relies on venom and water-based maneuvers.

mechanisms: Transparent body making it difficult to target clearly in water
Liquid Ooze ability to damage opponents trying to drain HP

limitations: Dries out and struggles if removed from water for extended periods

feats.claim: Fired toxic beams from its red eyes to damage port facilities.

campaignTags.claim: Naturally lives and fights in aquatic environments

unknowns: Exact toxicity potency of individual stings on larger human targets.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Tentacruel extends massive numbers of stinging tentacles to ensnare opponents and inject potent toxins. It commands significant destructive presence near oceans and water bodies.

mechanisms: High special defense
Rigid crystalline red orbs that absorb some energy impacts

limitations: Vulnerable to sudden physical trauma on land

sources.supports: Tentacle combat capabilities, moveset, and stats

feats.claim: A giant specimen demolished skyscrapers using its extended tentacles and energy beams.

campaignTags.claim: Swims proficiently through deep ocean waters

unknowns: Maximum extension length of all eighty tentacles simultaneously.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Vaporeon melts into water to elude detection and launches surging aquatic attacks. It uses its finned tail to propel itself with high agility in aquatic combat.

mechanisms: Water absorption ability to heal from water-type attacks
Cellular structure allowing it to liquefy and hide in water

limitations: Dependent on moisture or water bodies for its full stealth and liquefaction abilities

sources.supports: Cellular liquefaction, water moveset, and weaknesses

feats.claim: Completely dissolved its physical body into water to evade an incoming attack.
feats.citation: Pokémon anime episode: 'The Battling Eevee Brothers'

campaignTags.claim: Aqua Ring restores health over time

unknowns: Duration it can maintain its liquid form without returning to a solid shape.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Venomoth flutters through the air, shedding toxic scales that induce various status conditions such as sleep or poison. It combines airborne harassment with subtle psychic and bug-type attacks.

mechanisms: Shed scales acting as a smokescreen or deterrent
Compound Eyes ability ensuring high move accuracy

limitations: Wings are fragile and easily damaged by heavy wind or water blasts

feats.claim: Released a thick cloud of paralyzing and sleep-inducing scales across a forest clearing.

unknowns: Exact chemical composition of the varied colored wing scales.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Venonat uses its large compound eyes as radar to track targets in the dark, defending itself with poison powder emitted from its small, furry body.

mechanisms: Compound Eyes ability
Thick fur coating absorbing minor impacts

limitations: Slow physical movement speed on the ground

sources.supports: Sensory eye features, powder attacks, and weaknesses

feats.claim: Used its compound eyes to track invisible or hidden targets in total darkness.
feats.citation: Pokémon anime episode: 'March of the Exeggutor Squad'

unknowns: Whether its eye structure can perceive ultraviolet wavelengths outside standard conditions.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Venusaur anchors its heavy bulk to the ground, absorbing solar energy through the large plant on its back to unleash powerful beams and release debilitating spores.

mechanisms: Thick, resilient hide
Thorn-covered body deterring physical grapples

limitations: Solar Beam requires a charging turn unless bright sunlight is active

sources.supports: Solar energy utilization, combat stats, and moveset

feats.claim: Absorbed ambient sunlight to instantly fire a concentrated beam of solar energy.

campaignTags.claim: Synthesis allows it to recover health using sunlight

unknowns: Upper weight limit of objects it can lift with its vine whips.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Sword and Shield / Generation VIII
characters.summary: Gigantamax Venusaur towers over battlefields like a colossal mountain, using the giant flower on its back to generate cataclysmic gusts of pollen and massive energy torrents.

mechanisms: Immense physical mass
Thick barrier of swirling petals and turbulent wind generated by its size

limitations: Gigantamax transformation reverts automatically after three turns
characters.formDifferences: Increases size to titanic proportions, alters the flower on its back into a towering cloud-piercing structure, and grants access to G-Max Vine Lash.

sources.supports: Gigantamax form attributes, G-Max Vine Lash, and scale

feats.claim: Generated violent gales capable of blowing away entire squads of opposing Pokémon with a flap of its gigantic flower petals.
feats.citation: Pokémon Sword and Shield game lore / Gigantamax battle sequences

conditional.ability: Gigantamax form abilities and G-Max Vine Lash
conditional.dependsOn: Dynamax Energy and Gigantamax Band activation

campaignTags.claim: Gigantamax transformation grows the Pokémon to towering proportions
Gigantamax form provides massive physical scale

unknowns: Exact structural integrity of terrain under sustained Gigantamax tremors.

characters.continuity: Pokémon X and Y / Generation VI-IX core games
characters.summary: Mega Venusaur bolsters its defense with thick-skinned bark and the massive flower on its back, resisting damage while countering with heavy grass and poison moves.

mechanisms: Thick Fat ability reducing damage from Fire and Ice attacks
Reinforced floral armor shell

limitations: Requires the Venusaurite stone and active Mega Resonance to maintain the form
characters.formDifferences: Grows a second flower bloom on its forehead, increases overall body mass, gains the Thick Fat ability, and raises defensive stats.

sources.supports: Mega Evolution stats, Thick Fat ability, and defense profiles

feats.claim: Withstood direct super-effective fire blasts that would normally incapacitate standard Venusaur, thanks to its enhanced physiological defenses.
feats.citation: Pokémon X and Y official competitive battle demonstrations

conditional.ability: Mega Evolution form and Thick Fat damage reduction
conditional.dependsOn: Venusaurite held item and Trainer resonance

campaignTags.claim: Giga Drain absorbs opponent life force to restore health

unknowns: Maximum duration it can maintain Mega Evolution under extreme environmental heat.

characters.continuity: Pokémon Generation I-IX core games and anime
characters.summary: Victreebel hangs from tree branches, waiting to lure prey into its large, acid-secreting pouch with sweet-smelling nectar. It fights with vine whips and corrosive digestive fluids.

mechanisms: Waxy, acid-resistant outer skin
Ability to dissolve incoming organic projectiles with digestive fluids

limitations: Immobile while anchored to trees or ceilings by its vine stem

sources.supports: Acidic pouch capabilities, vine attacks, and weaknesses

feats.claim: Swallowed large objects and prey whole into its acidic stomach cavity.

unknowns: Composition of the sweet honey fragrance used to attract prey.
